sources.title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: What You Need to Know
sources.citationText: National Institute of Mental Health. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: What You Need to Know. NIH Publication No. 24-MH-3573. 2024.
sources.relevanceNote: Clinical symptom domains, presentation education, functional interference, alternative explanations, and separation of cognitive testing from diagnosis.

sources.title: Symptoms of ADHD
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
sources.citationText: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Symptoms of ADHD. Updated July 30, 2026.
sources.relevanceNote: Current presentation terminology and high-level symptom education.

sources.title: Diagnosing ADHD
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
sources.citationText: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Diagnosing ADHD. Updated July 30, 2026.
sources.relevanceNote: Diagnostic process, absence of a single test, and non-ADHD conditions that can produce similar symptoms.

sources.title: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: diagnosis and management (NG87)
sources.authorsOrOrganization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
sources.publicationType: Clinical guideline; last updated September 13, 2019; current page includes later amendments
sources.citationText: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: diagnosis and management. NG87. Published March 14, 2018; last updated September 13, 2019.
sources.relevanceNote: Formal diagnosis guardrails, impairment across settings, environmental modifications, structure, work/education/social functioning.

sources.title: Validity of the executive function theory of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: a meta-analytic review
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Willcutt EG, Doyle AE, Nigg JT, Faraone SV, Pennington BF
sources.citationText: Willcutt EG, Doyle AE, Nigg JT, Faraone SV, Pennington BF. Validity of the executive function theory of ADHD: a meta-analytic review. Biol Psychiatry. 2005;57(11):1336-1346. doi:10.1016/j.biopsych.2005.02.006.
sources.relevanceNote: Executive-function constructs including vigilance, working memory, planning and response inhibition; explicitly shows heterogeneity and lack of necessity/sufficiency.

sources.title: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and working memory in adults: a meta-analytic review
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Alderson RM, Kasper LJ, Hudec KL, Patros CHG
sources.citationText: Alderson RM, Kasper LJ, Hudec KL, Patros CHG. ADHD and working memory in adults: a meta-analytic review. Neuropsychology. 2013;27(3):287-302. doi:10.1037/a0032371.

sources.title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder and Behavioral Inhibition: A Meta-Analytic Review of the Stop-signal Paradigm
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Alderson RM, Rapport MD, Kofler MJ
sources.citationText: Alderson RM, Rapport MD, Kofler MJ. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder and Behavioral Inhibition: A Meta-Analytic Review of the Stop-signal Paradigm. J Abnorm Child Psychol. 2007;35(5):745-758. doi:10.1007/s10802-007-9131-6.
sources.relevanceNote: Response-inhibition evidence with an important specificity qualification.

sources.title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder and Monetary Delay Discounting: A Meta-Analysis of Case-Control Studies
sources.journalOrSeries: Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging 1(4):316–325
sources.citationText: Jackson JNS, MacKillop J. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder and Monetary Delay Discounting: A Meta-Analysis of Case-Control Studies. Biol Psychiatry Cogn Neurosci Neuroimaging. 2016;1(4):316-325. doi:10.1016/j.bpsc.2016.01.007.
sources.relevanceNote: Reward/delay-processing evidence; supports group-level association, not individual prediction.

sources.title: Emotion dysregulation in adults with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: a meta-analysis
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Beheshti A, Chavanon ML, Christiansen H
sources.citationText: Beheshti A, Chavanon ML, Christiansen H. Emotion dysregulation in adults with ADHD: a meta-analysis. BMC Psychiatry. 2020;20:120. doi:10.1186/s12888-020-2442-7.
sources.relevanceNote: Adult emotional-regulation association; not a formal diagnostic criterion.

sources.title: Evaluating vigilance deficits in ADHD: a meta-analysis of CPT performance
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Huang-Pollock CL, Karalunas SL, Tam H, Moore AN
sources.citationText: Huang-Pollock CL, Karalunas SL, Tam H, Moore AN. Evaluating vigilance deficits in ADHD: a meta-analysis of CPT performance. J Abnorm Psychol. 2012;121(2):360-371. doi:10.1037/a0027205.

sources.title: Reaction time variability in ADHD: a meta-analytic review of 319 studies
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Kofler MJ, Rapport MD, Sarver DE, Raiker JS, Orban SA, Friedman LM, Kolomeyer EG
sources.citationText: Kofler MJ, Rapport MD, Sarver DE, et al. Reaction time variability in ADHD: a meta-analytic review of 319 studies. Clin Psychol Rev. 2013;33(6):795-811. doi:10.1016/j.cpr.2013.06.001.
sources.relevanceNote: Experimental performance variability; also demonstrates limited specificity versus clinical controls.

sources.title: A systematic review on the association between ADHD and procrastination
sources.citationText: Suriano R. A systematic review on the association between ADHD and procrastination. Res Dev Disabil. 2026;175:105342. doi:10.1016/j.ridd.2026.105342.
sources.relevanceNote: Current review of ADHD–procrastination association; mechanisms remain uncertain and procrastination is transdiagnostic.

sources.title: The effects of acute stress on core executive functions: A meta-analysis and comparison with cortisol
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Shields GS, Sazma MA, Yonelinas AP
sources.citationText: Shields GS, Sazma MA, Yonelinas AP. The effects of acute stress on core executive functions: A meta-analysis and comparison with cortisol. Neurosci Biobehav Rev. 2016;68:651-668. doi:10.1016/j.neubiorev.2016.06.038.
sources.relevanceNote: Transdiagnostic evidence that acute stress can alter working memory, cognitive flexibility and aspects of inhibition.

sources.title: The impairments of sleep loss on core executive functions: General and task-specific effects
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Cao Y, Xie T, Ma N
sources.citationText: Cao Y, Xie T, Ma N. The impairments of sleep loss on core executive functions: General and task-specific effects. Sleep Med Rev. 2025;84:102163. doi:10.1016/j.smrv.2025.102163.
sources.relevanceNote: Non-specific sleep-loss effects on executive functions including inhibitory control and cognitive flexibility.

sources.title: Failures Due to Interruptions or Distractions: A Review and a New Framework
sources.citationText: Couffe C, Michael GA. Failures Due to Interruptions or Distractions: A Review and a New Framework. Am J Psychol. 2017;130(2):163-181. doi:10.5406/amerjpsyc.130.2.0163.
sources.relevanceNote: General, non-ADHD-specific interruption/distraction effects and task resumption.

sources.title: Do children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) have set shifting deficits?
sources.authorsOrOrganization: Irwin LN, Kofler MJ, Soto EF, Groves NB
sources.publicationType: Peer-reviewed experimental study with critical review of prior shifting literature
sources.citationText: Irwin LN, Kofler MJ, Soto EF, Groves NB. Do children with ADHD have set shifting deficits? Neuropsychology. 2019;33(4):470-481. doi:10.1037/neu0000546.
sources.relevanceNote: Supports conservative Moderate status for task switching/set shifting; highlights construct-validity and specificity limits.

sources.title: Motivation and cognitive control: from behavior to neural mechanism
sources.citationText: Botvinick M, Braver T. Motivation and cognitive control: from behavior to neural mechanism. Annu Rev Psychol. 2015;66:83-113. doi:10.1146/annurev-psych-010814-015044.
sources.relevanceNote: General motivation/reward–cognitive-control interaction; used only for non-specific contextual modulation, not as ADHD-specific evidence.
